title: Multihump-Multivalley Soliton Families on a Plane Wave Background in Birefringent Optical Fibers
abstract: We obtain a family of multihump-multivalley solitons (MHMVSs) on a plane-wave background in birefringent optical fibers governed by the two-component Fokas-Lenells equations, with exact solutions derived via the Darboux transformation method. The fundamental solutions are systematically classified through their phase diagrams, and higher-order configurations are identified as well. Notably, the construction extends to solitons with arbitrary MHMV structures, a class of solutions previously unreported in two-component integrable systems. Numerical simulations confirm the robustness of these solutions under weak white noise. Furthermore, analysis of their topological structure reveals that the virtual monopole field is determined equally by the intensity zeros and poles of MHMVSs in the complex plane, a feature that has remained unrecognized in previous studies of nonlinear wave topological phases. These findings reveal a previously unknown soliton family on a plane-wave background along with a distinct topological feature within the two-component framework, thereby enriching the broader understanding of topological phases of nonlinear waves.
summary: This paper presents the discovery of a previously unknown family of multihump-multivalley solitons (MHMVSs) using the Darboux transformation method on birefringent optical fibers. The research establishes that these solutions possess distinct topological characteristics, notably linking the virtual monopole field to both intensity zeros and poles in the complex plane.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically derive and analyze multihump-multivalley soliton (MHMVS) families existing on a plane wave background within birefringent optical fibers.
main_result: The authors obtained exact solutions for MHMVSs, including arbitrary configurations (AMHMVSs), demonstrating a previously unknown soliton family and revealing that the virtual monopole field is equally determined by intensity zeros and poles.
method: Exact solutions were derived using the Darboux transformation method applied to the two-component Fokas-Lenells equations. Stability was confirmed via numerical simulations under weak white noise.
model_or_system: The physical system modeled is birefringent optical fibers, governed by the integrable two-component Fokas-Lenells equations (CFL equations). This system is an extension of the Manakov model incorporating self-steepening and spatio-temporal coupling effects.
key_observables: Multihump-Multivalley Solitons (MHMVSs), Arbitrary MHMVSs (AMHMVSs), virtual monopole field, intensity profiles (e.g., cube, star, hexagonal patterns).
important_parameters: Birefringence parameters ($\eta$), background wave amplitude ($a_s$), and spectral parameters ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to solitons propagating on a plane wave background, contrasting with previous work limited to vanishing backgrounds.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates example intensity structures of MHMVSs on the plane wave, showing various patterns like cube, star, hexagonal, and triangular configurations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives solutions using the Darboux transformation method, classifies fundamental solutions via phase diagrams, analyzes the topological structure related to the virtual monopole field, and confirms stability through numerical simulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for theoretical physicists in quantum optics and open quantum systems as it provides new exact analytical solutions (MHMVSs) and reveals novel topological features within a coupled nonlinear wave system framework.
